incidents.vector: Account takeover of BlueSky profiles to post pro-Kremlin and anti-Ukraine propaganda since April.
incidents.impact: Multiple BlueSky accounts compromised and used to push Russian disinformation; BlueSky has been suspending affected accounts until owners can resecure them.

incidents.victim: Central Asian telecom providers (Afghanistan, Kazakhstan, Turkey, India, Donbas)
incidents.vector: Stealthy Linux post-exploitation framework deployed on telco infrastructure with LAN scanning to reach air-gapped systems.
incidents.impact: Multiple Chinese threat clusters have used the framework against ISPs and telcos for years with zero VirusTotal detections; PwC links activity to the Calypso (Red Lamassu) APT alongside Windows backdoors.

incidents.victim: RXNT (healthcare e-prescription platform) — including US Congress members
incidents.vector: Network intrusion at healthcare software vendor; technical details not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Patient prescription data stolen, including records of US Congress members who use RXNT; company notified authorities on the final day allowed under US health privacy laws.

incidents.victim: High-profile individuals in Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea
incidents.vector: Compromised home Wi-Fi routers with DNS hijacking to redirect dictionary software updates to a malicious server; trojanized SumatraPDF binary deploying Cobalt Strike, Merlin/Apollo Agents, and a new C6DOOR backdoor.
incidents.impact: Expansion of a long-running Chinese APT into personal devices outside the office; an exposed S3 bucket revealed 48 staged files and phishing pages mimicking Signal authentication.

incidents.vector: CISA contractor (Nightwing) published a private repository of plaintext credentials to a public GitHub account, including admin keys to three AWS GovCloud accounts and dozens of internal CISA system passwords.
incidents.impact: AWS GovCloud admin tokens and plaintext logins for CISA Landing Zone DevSecOps and Artifactory systems exposed; CISA says no sensitive data has been confirmed compromised; Senate Homeland Security Committee has demanded a classified briefing.

incidents.attacker: North Korea — suspected state-linked criminal group
incidents.vector: Employee device compromised via a poisoned Nx Console VS Code extension (downstream of the TanStack supply chain attack).
incidents.impact: Approximately 3,800 internal GitHub repositories exfiltrated and offered for sale on a cybercrime forum for $50,000; critical secrets rotated; GitHub says no customer data was affected and that the incident was contained.

incidents.victim: npm ecosystem (TanStack, Mistral AI, UiPath, OpenSearch, @antv, echarts-for-react and 169+ downstream packages)
incidents.attacker: North Korea — suspected state-linked criminal group
incidents.vector: Chained GitHub Actions abuse (pwn-request, cache poisoning, OIDC token extraction from runner memory) on TanStack CI to publish signed packages with valid SLSA Build Level 3 provenance; separate @antv maintainer-account compromise published malicious data-visualization libraries that ran a 499KB obfuscated payload during npm install.
incidents.impact: 640 malicious packages removed and 61,274 npm tokens revoked; payload steals credentials across GitHub, AWS, HashiCorp Vault, npm, Kubernetes and 1Password; more than 2,200 'Shai-Hulud: We Go Again' victim repos observed; Grafana and others confirmed downstream compromise.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to 7-Eleven systems used to store franchisee documents, consistent with the Salesforce data-theft pattern used by ShinyHunters.
incidents.impact: Names, addresses, and Social Security numbers of franchisee personnel stolen; breach discovered April 8, disclosed to state regulators this week; FBI has issued guidance urging ShinyHunters victims not to pay ransom.

incidents.vector: Malware (LameHug, ScopeCreep) embedding open-source LLMs to generate system commands dynamically on infected hosts, bypassing static detection; AI-enhanced phishing and Ukrainian-language voice deepfakes targeting service members.
incidents.impact: Ukrainian National Security and Defense Council reports a growing offense-defense imbalance; Russian operators are routinely using ChatGPT, Gemini, and self-hosted Llama for reconnaissance, exploit development, and recruitment of saboteurs.

incidents.victim: Pierre & Vacances, Belambra, Gîtes de France (French holiday booking)
incidents.vector: Network intrusion details not disclosed; the same actor 'ChimeraZ' claimed all three.
incidents.impact: Stolen customer data from three French holiday booking platforms put up for sale online.

incidents.vector: Cross-chain bridge exploit; technical details not yet published.
incidents.impact: $11.58 million in crypto assets stolen from the Verus-Ethereum bridge.

incidents.victim: Government of the Northern Mariana Islands (US territory)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack on government email infrastructure; officials have not confirmed whether ransomware was involved.
incidents.impact: Email servers disrupted, slowing administrative operations across the territorial government.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of authentication bypass CVE-2026-20182 in SD-WAN Controller/Manager; multiple clusters separately chain CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122 using the public ZeroZenX 'XenShell' JSP webshell.
incidents.impact: UAT-8616 added SSH keys, modified NETCONF, and escalated to root; ten post-compromise clusters deployed Godzilla/Behinder webshells, Cobalt Strike, Sliver, AdaptixC2, Mythic, and XMRig miners; infrastructure overlaps with operational relay box (ORB) networks.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion; technical entry vector not yet disclosed by Foxconn.
incidents.impact: Nitrogen ransomware group claims theft of 8TB of data including confidential chip designs and project files for Apple, Google, and NVIDIA orders; North American factory operations disrupted.
